text:
The Maple Leafs' losing streak reached nine games before Monday's win on Long Island, and somewhere in it Auston Matthews stopped being diplomatic. Headlines had the captain calling the play "Inexcusable" (Bleacher Report) and saying "We should be embarrassed" (The Times of India). Now the talk around him is about his future, with Elliotte Friedman quoted as saying "All bets are off" and another insider saying he'd be "shocked" by an in-season trade.

The strange part is that Matthews himself has been very good. He has 34 points in 26 games, and his 14 goals came on 13.2 expected, so the finishing is honest. Toronto has 55.5% of 5v5 expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on the ice. The caveat is the assists: the team has scored 11.8 more goals than its chances deserve while he's out there, which pads his total. Evolving-Hockey had him facing the other team's best with weak help last season. Our numbers project about 93 points. Whether Toronto can build something worthy of that is the question hanging over the season.
headline: Auston Matthews is great on a team that isn't
